Features

Everything a service needs, in one window

The operator window follows the workflow churches already know: the schedule on the left, preview in the middle, live on the right, and the library along the bottom.

Schedule

An ordered service list. Drag items to rearrange, add notes, save the service and reopen it next week. Services save in the open .twp format.

Preview and Live

See a slide before anyone else does. Send it live with one click or with Page Down, then step through its slides from the live column.

Songs

Lyrics with verse, chorus and bridge structure. Search by title, author or a lyric line. Online lyrics search is built in, and results are clearly marked as community contributions, not rights cleared lyrics.

Scriptures

Look up a passage by reference, or search by words so every typed word must appear in the reference or the text. The King James Version and World English Bible work offline, and a + button adds a scripture by hand.

Media

Images, videos and backgrounds behind lyrics or verses. A built in set of photos and motion loops is included, and you can add your own photos and videos.

Themes and layouts

Reusable themes with a display font per theme, bold text, and slide layouts including Full Screen, Lower Third, Upper Third, Left Panel and Centre Card. Preview and projector always match.

Live output

A projector window on the second screen, with an output monitor picker, fullscreen and always on top. If the projector is unplugged, output falls back to the main display. NDI output publishes the live output as a named source for OBS and vMix.

Logo, Black and Clear

One click blanking and logo display, right on the toolbar, for the moments between items.

Alerts

Short messages over the live output, including a scrolling marquee strip at the top, at slow, normal or fast speed, until hidden.

Keyboard shortcuts

The shortcuts worship operators already use: Page Down goes live, Ctrl+B blacks the screen, Ctrl+L shows the logo, arrow keys step through slides and schedule items. A shortcuts dialog lists them all.

Light and dark

Light, Dark and System themes. System follows the operating system and keeps following it.

Content API

Bible versions and passages come from bible-api.com, public domain translations only, one slide per verse. Nothing copyrighted is bundled.

Who it is for

Built for the whole team

Different people run different parts of a service. True Worship gives each of them what they need in the same window.

Media team

One window for schedule, preview and live, with an output monitor picker and NDI for the livestream.

Worship leaders

Build the service order, and see every lyric and verse before it goes out.

Volunteers

A layout that follows the conventions operators already know, a shortcuts dialog, and preview before live, so mistakes stay private.

Pastors

Scriptures with their references on screen, alerts for announcements, and Logo, Black and Clear for the moments between items.

How it works

One afternoon to a full service

Four steps, and the service is ready to run.

1

Build the schedule

Add songs, scriptures, media and custom items in service order. Drag to rearrange.

2

Preview the slide

Click any slide to see exactly how it will look on the projector, background and theme included.

3

Go live

One click, or Page Down, sends the slide to the projector. Logo, Black and Clear are one click away.

4

Step through

Move through verses and slides from the live column, or with the arrow keys, while the congregation sees only the output.

Moving over

Bring your whole Sunday with you

True Worship is built so a church can move a whole Sunday over in one afternoon, and verify the move before Sunday, not during it.

EasyWorship schedules

Import .ews schedule files, which are ZIP archives, and read the schedule structure directly.

EasyWorship song libraries

Import song databases including Songs.db and SongWords.dat, following the documented open source importer path.

OpenSong and OpenLyrics

Import OpenSong and OpenLyrics song files, so churches coming from any free tool are covered too.

Open export

Songs, schedules and themes export to open JSON, so nobody is ever locked in again.

Import is under active work: the formats above are covered, and full fidelity EasyWorship library import is being finished against real sample files.

Community Songbook

The feature no free tool owns yet

Churches contribute and correct lyrics, and updates sync to everyone. This matters most for Nigerian songs, which no shared library covers well today.

Edits sync to everyone

A church fixes a line, adds a verse or adds a translation, and the edit reaches the shared library as a new version.

Full version history

Every song keeps its history, so a bad edit can be rolled back in one click.

Moderation

New songs and edits from new contributors sit in a review queue until trusted editors approve them, and any user can report a wrong or copyrighted lyric.

Contributor credit

Every song shows its contributors and source church, so the community, not an anonymous database, gets the credit.

Copyright guardrails

Contributors confirm they own the lyric, it is public domain, or they have permission to share it. A CCLI number field lets licensed churches record the licence. Modern commercial songs without permission are refused.

Offline first

Every church keeps a full local copy. Sync happens when there is internet, and a service never depends on it.

The Songbook tab is already in the app. The sync service that shares edits between churches is the next phase of work.

Content and licensing

Only what the licence allows, always labelled

Every song and Bible in True Worship carries a source field: public domain, owned, licensed or community. Copyrighted material is never bundled without permission or a licence.

Bibles, offline

The King James Version and World English Bible are bundled, both public domain, so they work with no internet.

Nigerian languages

Downloadable packs from eBible.org include Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, Nigerian Pidgin, Fulfulde and other Nigerian languages. Each translation ships with its own licence note, and the app only bundles what the licence allows.

Bring your own translation

CrossWire SWORD modules can be imported, so churches can use translations they already own.

Copyrighted versions

Versions like NIV, ESV, NKJV, NLT and NASB are never bundled or redistributed. They stay reachable only through a licensed lookup route, under those services own terms.

Hymns

The seed library is public domain hymns, each text stating its public domain status. As a rule, copyright generally expires 70 years after the writer's death. Anything newer needs permission or a licence.

The legal route for modern songs

For copyrighted lyrics, paste your own lyrics or import through a CCLI SongSelect licence. That is the legal route for licensed churches.

Get it

Run it from source today, installers are coming

Installers for Windows, Linux and macOS are the final release phase. Until then, the app runs from source in a few commands.

git clone https://github.com/toluwanibakare/true-worship.git
cd true-worship
npm install
npm run backgrounds   # generate the built-in set, once after cloning
npm run build         # typecheck + production build
npm run electron      # run the built desktop app

For development, npm run electron:dev runs the full desktop app with operator and projector windows, and npm run dev runs the frontend in a browser for UI work only.

FAQ

Questions churches ask

Is True Worship really free?

Yes. It is free forever and open source under GPL-3.0. There is no subscription, no trial and no paid tier.

Which platforms does it run on?

Windows, Linux and macOS, from one codebase. The operator window runs on the laptop and the live output window goes to the projector.

Does it work without internet?

Yes. Songs, Bibles, schedules and themes live on disk in a local database. Online lookups and songbook sync are extras, never requirements for a service.

Can we move from EasyWorship?

That is the plan. Import covers .ews schedules, song databases, OpenSong and OpenLyrics files, with full fidelity library import being finished against real sample files. Everything also exports to open JSON.

What about copyrighted songs and Bibles?

Only public domain, owned or licensed content is bundled, and every item is labelled with its source. Modern songs need permission or a CCLI SongSelect licence, and copyrighted Bible versions are never bundled.

Will it have Nigerian language Bibles?

Yes, through downloadable eBible.org packs including Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, Nigerian Pidgin and Fulfulde, each with its own licence note.

When do installers arrive?

Installers for Windows, Linux and macOS are the final release phase, along with docs and the first public launch to Nigerian churches. Until then, run from source with the commands above.

Ready to run your next service on it?

Free forever, open source, on Windows, Linux and macOS. Get the source and run it from the commands above.
